BiblicalUsage: Cherpah is reproach, the shame laid on a person or a people, and Scripture shows God both sending it and taking it away. Rachel says God has taken away her reproach, David asks who will take away the reproach of Israel, Nehemiah calls the people to rebuild so they will be a reproach no more, and the psalmist lays his own reproach before God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God is the one who removes reproach, and no shame I carry is beyond His taking away. I hold that the cross is where every reproach ends, because Christ bore ours there.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
